chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Muskān from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding the man who raises his hands whenever he inclines for bowing and prostration, and whenever he raises his head from bowing or prostration, he said: 'It is servitude (or worship).'

key_terms.الْعُبُودِيَّةُ: Servitude or worship, indicating the spiritual nature of the act

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of raising hands during prayer transitions in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the act of raising hands during the transitions of bowing and prostration is identified as 'al-Abudiyyah' (servitude), emphasizing the physical manifestation of humility before God. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that such movements are not merely mechanical but are profound expressions of worship and submission, distinguishing the spiritual quality of the prayer. The term underscores the believer's conscious acknowledgment of their status as a servant, aligning physical action with inner devotion.
